https://www.breakingnews.ie/world/tate-b.text: Advertisement world Tate brothers remain in jail at least two more weeks as they fight extradition 27/07/2026 - 19:20 PM Tate Brothers Share this article By David Fischer, Associated Press Prefer BreakingNews.ie on Google Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate will remain in jail at least two more weeks until their next hearing as they fight extradition to the United Kingdom, where the brothers are accused of rape and sex trafficking, a federal judge said. US magistrate Lauren Louis set a detention hearing for August 13 to determine whether the Tates should stay in jail or be released during what could be a months-long extradition process. Advertisement The Tates were not in court on Monday or required to be there and have remained in jail since making a brief court appearance two days after their July 18 arrest. The Tates promote wealth, male dominance and misogyny through their social media empire and are among the world’s most polarising internet personalities. Attorney Joseph McBride, representing Andrew and Tristan Tate (Lynne Sladky/AP) The former professional kickboxers, who have dual US and UK citizenship, have millions of social media followers and are vocal supporters of US President Donald Trump. The White House has said the brothers should not expect any help from the president. Asked on Thursday whether the White House would intervene in the extradition process, press secretary Karoline Leavitt flatly rejected the idea. Advertisement The Tates’ attorney, Joseph McBride, said after last week’s hearing that they should remain in the US. “We are of course objecting to extradition because Andrew and Tristan are innocent,” Mr McBride said. “They’ve never done nothing wrong. They shouldn’t be extradited for crimes they did not commit.” Mr McBride said the extradition attempt is politically motivated and suggested the case involved former British prime minister Sir Keir Starmer’s decision to step down, though he provided no details. Prosecutors in Britain said the new charges relate to four new accusers and were brought after authorities received evidence from police in Bedfordshire. The allegations, which span from 2010 to 2017, include rape, assault, trafficking and offences relating to “indecent images of a child and extreme pornography”. Mr McBride said none of the latest accusers have been identified. The brothers are already charged with rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other accusers in the UK between 2012 and 2015. Advertisement The new allegations are the latest in a long-running international legal saga involving the Tates that has spanned the US, Britain and Romania. The brothers have repeatedly denied wrongdoing. The brothers moved to Romania in 2016 and were arrested there in 2022, accused of participating in schemes to lure women for sexual exploitation. They denied those allegations, and the Romanian case has not gone forward because of legal and procedural problems. Travel restrictions were lifted last year, and they flew to Florida. Andrew Tate, 39, became known a decade ago when he was a contestant on the UK reality television show Big Brother. He was booted from the show when a video appeared to show him assaulting a woman. He has amassed more than 10 million followers on X but has been banned from other platforms, including YouTube, TikTok and Instagram, for violating hate speech guidelines. He has made widely condemned comments, such as saying women who are sexually assaulted should bear some responsibility for the attacks and sharing graphic descriptions of how he might attack women. The Tate brothers have consistently denied allegations of abuse and human trafficking, claiming their violent and misogynistic statements have been taken out of context or were intended as jokes. https://telex.hu/english/2026/09/10/russ.text: Menü Kereső Russian Embassy reacts to news of Latvian-Hungarian energy talks with resentful post English Pupli Anna Sára Andrea Horváth Kávai (translation) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom “We took note of the Hungarian Foreign Minister, Anita Orbán’s statement, according to which matters of ‘energy cooperation’ were also on the agenda during her most recent meeting with her Latvian counterpart,” the Russian Embassy in Budapest wrote in a rather offended-sounding post on Thursday. Anita Orbán posted on Wednesday that she had held talks with Latvian Foreign Minister Baiba Braže—according to which they also agreed to resume consultations relating to foreign policy and security policy, which have been suspended between the two countries since 2019. Anita Orbán also announced that Hungary would participate in the defense of the Baltic airspace for the fifth time in 2028. Her post included the following passage, which is what the Russian Embassy took issue with: “The next step, in collaboration with the Ministry of Economy, will be to organize a new Latvian–Hungarian business forum in Hungary and to further develop the fintech partnerships that have already been launched. In the energy sector, we see particular potential in the field of energy storage, as Latvia has gained significant experience in this area, with some Hungarian companies already involved in the development of the Baltic energy system.” In its post, the Russian Embassy writes that the Hungarian side surely knows that Russia is also open to consultations with Budapest on all aspects of bilateral energy cooperation. And then comes the really interesting part: “However, if the Hungarian government believes it has found a new strategic energy partner in Riga, we can only wish both countries the best of luck in this regard. We hope that, as a result of their fruitful cooperation, first-class Baltic crude oil and natural gas will flow into Hungary—seasoned with the unparalleled aroma of freedom and liberal democracy.” The Russian Embassy’s heated response is particularly interesting in light of the events of the past few days. It was announced Tuesday morning that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had expelled 10 staff members of the Russian Embassy from Hungary. Foreign Minister Anita Orbán, however, also said that this does not mean a severing of diplomatic relations with Russia, as well as that Hungary intends to continue the necessary dialogue based on mutual respect and adherence to the rules. In response to the news, the spokesperson for the Russian Foreign Ministry promised a “harsh and painful” response. “First of all, we will do the same. But Hungary’s decision could also lead to a decrease in the number of joint economic projects with Russia,” Alexey Chepa, vice chairman of the State Duma’s Committee on International Affairs told the Russian news agency TASS. The Russian Embassy responded to the expulsion by saying that the new Hungarian government “has fallen prey to ideologically motivated, anti-Russian rhetoric, and that the Hungarian side’s statements about maintaining channels of dialogue with Russia and continuing pragmatic cooperation are worthless.” András Rácz, the Deputy Director General of the Hungarian Institute of International Affairs explained to Telex that according to the rules of diplomatic terminology, the Foreign Minister's statement implies that the ten Russian diplomats expelled from Hungary were in fact working under diplomatic cover and engaging in intelligence activities. https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/gen.text: SECRET MOSCOW MISSION: Senior White House Officials Kept In Dark About CIA Director’s Russia Trip August 28, 2026 1:30 pm No Comments President Donald Trump personally dispatched CIA Director John Ratcliffe on a highly secretive diplomatic mission to Moscow, with the trip kept so closely guarded that even senior White House officials and military leaders who would normally receive such briefings were not informed, according to The Wall Street Journal. Ratcliffe reportedly traveled aboard a U.S. military C-17 aircraft to Latvia before continuing into Russia. His arrival surprised European allies, who had not been informed in advance of the unusual mission. During meetings with Russian security officials, Ratcliffe delivered a clear message that the United States remains fully committed to NATO’s Article 5 collective-defense provision, under which an attack on one member is considered an attack on all. He also warned Moscow against launching attacks on NATO countries. Ratcliffe also discussed reviving peace negotiations with Ukraine in an effort to bring the war to an end. At the same time, he pressed Russian officials to avoid deepening economic or security ties with Iran as the Trump administration continues its sanctions campaign against Tehran. Trump later downplayed concerns that Russian President Vladimir Putin could order an attack against NATO allies and described Ratcliffe’s journey as “semi-routine.” The mission follows previous diplomatic efforts by Trump administration envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner that failed to halt the fighting, as Russia continued escalating its attacks and strengthening cooperation with Iran. Experts cited in the report said Ratcliffe’s experience using intelligence channels and negotiating the release of Americans held overseas made him a potentially effective envoy to communicate directly with the Kremlin while reinforcing that Trump’s peace efforts do not come at the expense of America’s security commitments to Europe. https://www.politico.eu/article/carneys-.text: STRASSBURG - Mark Carney nutzte eine Rede vor dem Europäischen Parlament, um zu skizzieren, was Ottawa sich von engeren Beziehungen zur EU erhoffen würde. Allerdings stellte er sich nicht uneingeschränkt hinter Ursula von der Leyens überraschenden Vorstoß eines „assoziierten Mitgliedstaats“. Einen Tag, nachdem der Kommissionspräsident diesen bislang einzigartigen Beziehungsstatus ins Spiel gebracht hatte, nahm der kanadische Premierminister das Angebot zur Kenntnis und nannte – anstatt es sofort anzunehmen – mögliche einzelne Bereiche der Zusammenarbeit, darunter kritische Mineralien, Verteidigung, KI, Energiesicherheit und Raumfahrt. Er forderte außerdem einen reibungsloseren digitalen Handel mit nicht-landwirtschaftlichen Waren und Dienstleistungen sowie die Teilnahme Kanadas am Erasmus+-Programm, dem Studentenaustauschprogramm der EU. Advertisement Advertisement „Wir begrüßen dieses Ziel“, sagte er mit Blick auf von der Leyens Vorschlag. „Umfragen zeigen, dass eine überwältigende Mehrheit der Kanadier deutlich engere Beziehungen befürwortet.“ Carneys Liste potenzieller Bündnisse war ein früher Versuch, einem bislang noch weitgehend undefinierten politischen Vorhaben konkrete Inhalte zu verleihen. Die Idee eines „assoziierten Mitglieds“ hatte am Mittwoch für Verwirrung gesorgt, da die Kommission dies zuvor nicht mit den europäischen Hauptstädten abgestimmt hatte und ein solcher Status derzeit nicht existiert. Später am Mittwoch erklärte US-Präsident Donald Trump, er könnte mit „erheblichen Zöllen“ reagieren, sollte Kanada eine engere Anbindung an die EU anstreben. „Ein Bündnis für die Zukunft ist ein einzigartiger, positiver Ansatz, den wir gemeinsam definieren werden, indem wir auf unseren gemeinsamen Stärken aufbauen und uns auf gemeinsame Werte stützen“, sagte Carney. Ministerin Joly will Zölle vermeiden Kanadas Wirtschaftsministerin Mélanie Joly deutete am Mittwoch gegenüber Reportern in Toronto an, dass Ottawa zusätzliche Garantien im Handelsbereich anstrebt – was möglicherweise neue Gesetze erfordern könnte. Auf die Frage nach der Möglichkeit einer „assoziierten“ EU-Mitgliedschaft merkte Joly an, dass Länder mit Freihandelsabkommen dazu neigen, sich stärker abzuschotten, um ihre eigenen Industrien zu schützen, wenn sie mit Zöllen belegt werden. Sie hob insbesondere die EU hervor. Advertisement Advertisement „Wir wollen sicherstellen, dass die Märkte zwischen uns weiterhin offen bleiben und dass nicht nur ein Freihandelsabkommen Bestand hat, sondern dass wir auch unsere Industriepolitik aufeinander abstimmen, insbesondere in den von den Zöllen betroffenen Sektoren“, sagte sie. „Das ist wirklich wichtig.“ Kanadas Parlament dürfte mitmischen In einer Pressekonferenz im Anschluss an seine Rede wurde Carney gefragt, ob die kanadische Bevölkerung bei der assoziierten Mitgliedschaft mitreden könne. Er antwortete: „Natürlich. Es wird Debatten geben, und es wird eine Abstimmung im kanadischen Parlament geben, aber zum jetzigen Zeitpunkt ist dies erst der Anfang des Prozesses.“ Carneys Eingeständnis, dass es im Parlament letztendlich zu Abstimmungen über diese „Allianz für die Zukunft“ mit der EU kommen wird, schien darauf hinzudeuten, dass die kanadischen Abgeordneten ein Mitspracherecht bei den Plänen des Teams des Premierministers erhalten werden. Das Unterhaus kehrt am Montag aus der Sommerpause zurück. Bevor von der Leyen die Bezeichnung „assoziiertes Mitglied“ fallen ließ, teilte Carney kanadischen Reportern mit, dass es in Straßburg keine „große Enthüllung“ geben werde. „Die eigentliche Vertiefung und die Diskussionen werden mit unserem Gipfeltreffen in Montreal … gegen Ende Oktober beginnen“, sagte er am Dienstag in Toronto am Rande seines globalen Investitionsgipfels. „Und dann geht es von dort aus weiter.“ Europa hat für die Regierung Carney höchste Priorität, da die EU als der einfachste Weg für Kanada angesehen wird, die bestehenden Freihandelsbeziehungen zu vertiefen – ein Thema, das bereits vor einem Jahrzehnt im Parlament diskutiert wurde. Advertisement Advertisement Nun stehen die Verantwortlichen in Kanada und der EU unter Druck, ihre lange Liste an Aufgaben abzuarbeiten, bevor sie in Montreal eintreffen, um Fortschritte in einer Reihe von Bereichen zu demonstrieren – von Handel und Rüstungsbeschaffung bis hin zu KI und Supercomputing. Der designierte Botschafter bei der EU, Jonathan Wilkinson, erklärte gegenüber POLITICO, das Ziel des EU-Kanada-Gipfels bestehe darin, „eine Reihe sehr konkreter Maßnahmen“ zu erarbeiten, die im Laufe des nächsten Jahres umgesetzt werden sollen. „Wir wollen dabei sehr ehrgeizig vorgehen.“ Dieser Artikel wurde aktualisiert. Zi-Ann Lum und Sue Allan haben aus Ottawa zu diesem Artikel beigetragen. Er erschien zuerst auf Englisch bei POLITICO.

Photograph: Benoît Tessier/Reuters Protest Explainer Why are people protesting across Europe? A summary of why the protests started and how governments have responded to them Arrests over France protests rise to 1,800, with whole streets in Paris ‘devastated’ – Europe live Harry Taylor Sun 18 Oct 2026 11.15 EDT Last modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 11.16 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Young people have been taking to the streets in countries across Europe, including Spain, France and Portugal , to protest over their unhappiness at the state of schools and wider cost of living crisis. In France, high school pupils have clashed with police in often violent protests over long hours, missing teachers, dilapidated classrooms and an opaque university admissions system. Pupils routinely miss months of teaching due to unfilled staff absences. Other demonstrators have then joined student marches to voice their unhappiness about rising living costs, including over fuel prices after US bombing caused the effective closure of the strait of Hormuz. The General Confederation of Labour (CGT), one of France’s largest unions, has backed the protests and called for lower prices, higher pensions and boosted wages. French president Emmanual Macron is nearing the end of his time in the Élysée Palace after serving two terms. Over the Pyrenees in Spain , activists took to the streets in September over housing prices. They were triggered by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home after an investment fund hiked her rent by 230%. Maricarmen Abascal died a fortnight later after being admitted to hospital. Protesters have called for lower rents, an end to evictions and a ban on investment funds buying property. Similar pleas were made across the Iberian border in Portugal on Saturday, with hundreds gathering in central Lisbon. Portuguese housing prices rose by 124% between 2015 and 2024, roughly twice as fast as the EU average, according to official data. Squeezed household budgets were also at the centre of marches in Milan. A march on Saturday began peacefully but ended with masked rioters throwing stones, paving blocks and other objects at riot police and setting fire to barricades made from bar tables. Meanwhile, protests in Albania against the prime minister, Edi Rama, entered their sixth day on Sunday. Demonstrators have said they are unhappy with perceived corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards. When did protests start? The education protests in France began in late September, a week after the start of the school year. However, demonstrations have since intensified, reaching a high point on Saturday. Saturday was also the first day of cost of living protests in Italy, Portugal and Belgium. In Albania, protests have been taking place since the summer, triggered by a luxury coastal development backed by Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner. . Have they led to any changes? In France, the government has said it will deploy 3,000 more substitute teachers to deal with shortages, and include students in decision-making for schools. It also scrapped plans to increase some university registration fees, which it had announced for next year’s budget. Fuel protests in mid-September led to an announcement by the Elysee that the government would increase petrol subsidies for certain industries. Spain’s president, Pedro Sánchez, attempted to pass emergency housing legislation that would have protected tenants in the rental market. Socialist party leader Sanchez’s defeat led him to calling an early election for 29 November, as he told the public he needed a “broader progressive majority” to get the new laws through. Is there any sense it will end? Macron will give a televised address on Sunday night after holding a crisis meeting with key ministers. His interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, appeared to signal the French government are not willing to concede further, as he blamed “far left” protesters and “criminals who looted and ransacked” buildings across France. The country will go to the polls in April 2027. If Sanchez wins the Spanish election in November, and is able to pass the emergency housing legislation that was stymied last month, then marches in Spain could end. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/4233271..text: Home Azerbaijan Czech business eyes new opportunities along Middle Corridor - Interview Azerbaijan News 12 October 2026 09:29 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Czech Ministry of Transport Laman Zeynalova Deputy Editor-in-Chief Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 12. The Czech business eyes new opportunities along the Middle Corridor, Minister of Transport of the Czech Republic Ivan Bednárik said in an exclusive interview with Trend ahead of his visit to the South Caucasus and Central Asia. He pointed out that the South Caucasus and Central Asia are becoming increasingly important in connecting Europe and Asia, and the Czech Republic can offer expertise and technologies in rail transport, logistics, urban mobility and civil aviation. "My visit, accompanied by a business delegation, has a clear objective: to strengthen cooperation in transport and logistics and create new business opportunities for Czech companies and their potential partners in Azerbaijan, Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan. In all three countries, our programme therefore includes a series of ministerial meetings, business forums and meetings with representatives of state institutions and companies. Azerbaijan is a rapidly developing country with a stable political and economic environment. The opportunity to invest in such a country is welcome news for any investor," added the minister. Bednárik pointed out that in Azerbaijan, he wants to build on the memorandum that Minister Rashad Nabiyev and he signed in May this year and identify concrete steps for cooperation. "Our priorities are the development of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor, the modernisation of railways and urban transport, particularly the metro, the development of air connectivity and the implementation of modern transport technologies," the minister said. Czech perspective on Middle Corridor development The Czech minister noted that the Middle Corridor strengthens the resilience of supply chains between Europe and Asia. "Azerbaijan is an important regional partner for the Czech Republic. Transport is one of the key areas of our cooperation, particularly in the context of the growing importance of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, one of the main freight routes between Europe and Asia. From the Czech perspective, this corridor is important because it broadens our connections with the region and strengthens the resilience of supply chains between Europe and Asia. We therefore want to strengthen logistics links in this area and open up new opportunities for Czech companies. In addition to rail transport and urban mobility, we are also interested in opportunities for cooperation in aviation and modern transport technologies," Bednárik added. The minister noted that all the challenges related to the Middle Corridor in logistics, customs procedures and coordination are interconnected and need to be addressed comprehensively. "However, I consider eliminating bottlenecks, speeding up procedures and ensuring sufficient capacity at container and multimodal terminals to be essential. We also need to improve existing transport infrastructure, rather than relying on a single mode of transport, and provide alternative routes for moving goods. Tools to facilitate cross-border procedures and sufficient capacity at multimodal terminals are equally important. Logistics and freight transport will therefore be among the subjects of my discussions with Azerbaijani institutions, the EU Delegation in Baku and representatives of the transport sector," he explained. Bednárik noted that although the importance of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor is growing rapidly, its further development requires investment in infrastructure, the modernisation of logistics and customs processes, and closer cooperation among the countries along the entire route. "This also applies to the countries of the European Union. That is why, this spring, I initiated a European discussion on strengthening the competitiveness of rail freight and improving the coordination of international transport corridors. I am also working to address bottlenecks during the Czech presidency of the International Transport Forum (ITF) at the OECD. Creating a unified digital and logistics space with interoperable transport systems along European transport corridors will certainly be a lengthy process. It is important for the Czech Republic and Azerbaijan to cooperate and coordinate more closely in this area. This is something I want to emphasise through the agenda of my mission and cooperation involving Czech companies and researchers," he said. Transport cooperation beyond Middle Corridor Bednárik pointed out that he also sees considerable potential in urban and regional rail transport. "Czech companies have expertise in railway electrification, rolling stock, traffic management and modern technological solutions for aviation and rail transport. They also offer comprehensive solutions for urban mobility and air connectivity. We also see promising opportunities in zero-emission technologies, including hydrogen-powered transport, and in sustainable urban mobility through modern trainsets, metro trains and electric buses. This trend is developing rapidly in Europe. For example, the Czech company Škoda Group is one of Europe’s leading manufacturers of battery-powered trains and supplies many European countries. There are also successful Czech companies offering technologies for urban and suburban bus transport. A key topic for us is the modernisation of the Baku metro, where Škoda Group can offer its expertise. We also see opportunities in regional electric multiple units and the associated technical facilities," said the Czech minister. He believes that civil aviation is another promising area. "We want to discuss opportunities to develop direct air links between Baku and Prague, as well as cooperation in airport infrastructure, training and technologies for safe air traffic management. ERA, for example, could build on its existing activities in Azerbaijan," noted Bednárik. The minister went on to add that the Czech side sees considerable potential for closer cooperation with Azerbaijan in rail freight and logistics. "The CEO of ČD Cargo, the largest Czech rail freight operator, will be joining me in Baku. The company provides its services not only in the Czech Republic, but also in Slovakia, Hungary, Poland, Austria and Germany. We would also welcome discussions with our Azerbaijani partners on the possibility of establishing a joint logistics operator offering competitive door-to-door rates, coordinated multimodal services and simplified transit procedures," he added. Moreover, Bednárik pointed out that Czech rail operators, including ČD Cargo and EGT Express, as well as relevant industry and logistics associations, have extensive experience in international freight transport and could contribute to the development of integrated logistics services. "We also see prospects for new partnerships in air connectivity and urban mobility, which OMNIPOL Group and Škoda Group will present. The planned Czech-Azerbaijani business forum, to be held in Baku on 12 October, will provide a good opportunity to establish concrete business contacts," he concluded.
